jobs.description:
Epiroc is a leading productivity partner for the mining, infrastructure and natural resources industries. Using state-of-the-art technology, Epiroc develops and manufactures innovative drilling equipment and machinery for rock excavation and construction, as well as providing first-class service and consumables. The company was founded in Stockholm, Sweden. Its dedicated employees support and work closely with customers in more than 150 countries.

Do you want to make a real difference? Rock the future with a global player? Then join our team and get the ball rolling as a

Technical Product Specialist Smart Solutions (m/w/d)

Moving forward with inspiration

Key focus areas are

- Support the development, testing, and validation of innovative hydraulic attachment and smart machine solutions from concept through market launch.
- Participate in prototype assembly, field trials, product evaluations, and customer acceptance testing.
- Provide practical field feedback to Engineering, Product Management, and Service organizations to drive product improvements and customer-focused solutions.
- Assist customers and internal stakeholders in the successful adoption and deployment of smart technologies and digital solutions.
- Support root cause analysis and troubleshooting of new products and systems during field implementation.
- Execute service assignments, repairs, maintenance activities, commissioning, inspections, and troubleshooting at customer sites and in the workshop.
- Deliver technical training and operational guidance to customers and business partners.
- Provide professional technical advice regarding equipment operation, repairs, maintenance requirements, and spare parts recommendations.
- Prepare detailed and accurate service reports, machine condition assessments, and technical product reports.
- Support continuous improvement initiatives through the sharing of technical knowledge and field experience.

Strong skills

You are committed, like to take on responsibility and want to gain a deep insight into supply chain work. Ideally, you have the following skills:

- Completed technical vocational education or an equivalent qualification in mechanics, mechatronics, electrical engineering, hydraulics, or a related technical discipline.
- Strong knowledge of mechanical, hydraulic, electrical, and machine diagnostic systems.
- Experience within the mining, construction equipment, heavy machinery, or a related industry.
- Ability to diagnose technical issues and implement effective solutions in the field.
- Good understanding of common IT tools and digital service technologies.
- Experience with customer-facing technical service activities is highly desirable.
- Excellent German language skills, both written and spoken, together with basic English language skills.

More for you

Those who do a lot should also get a lot. That's why you'll benefit from an extensive range of offers that leaves almost nothing to be desired. And if you do? We are constantly working on expanding and improving our range of services - just get in touch. Here is a small excerpt of what you can expect:

Benefits in everyday working life

- Further training and development: you can still learn something with us

Career and studies

- Flexible working time models and home office options
- Gain experience in international cooperation, as you will be in regular contact with our global subsidiaries within the Epiroc Group
- Opportunity to gain professional experience parallel to your studies with the prospect of writing your thesis in an international environment

Health, sport and leisure

- Modern office equipment, free drinks
- Team events such as midsummer parties, workshops, barbecues and more

With united strength into the future

Have we inspired you? Then let's shape the future together: with innovation and commitment - and above all united. Simply apply online now via our career portal. Please let us know your earliest possible starting date.

We look forward to welcoming you to our team! We welcome applications from all people, regardless of their cultural and social background, age, religion, ideology, disability or sexual identity.

United. Inspired. Performance unites us, innovation inspires us and commitment drives us to develop further. In the 150 countries where you will find Epiroc, we encourage our employees to take responsibility for their own development and career with the support of their managers. We are committed to providing you with every opportunity to succeed in a culture of innovation, diversity and collaboration, combined with a caring atmosphere. Diversity and sustainability are key to developing fresh and innovative ideas and solutions for our customers. Epiroc is a leading manufacturer for the mining and infrastructure industry. Learn more at www.epirocgroup.com

It all starts with people. The world needs metals and minerals for the energy transition and our cities and infrastructure must be developed to serve a growing population. To succeed, we need to speed up the shift towards more sustainable mining and construction industries. We at Epiroc accelerate this transformation, together with customers and business partners in more than 150 countries, by developing and providing innovative and safe equipment, digital solutions, and aftermarket support.

All new thinkers are welcome. We are looking for those who want to develop, grow, and dare to think new. In Epiroc we attract, develop, and retain diverse talent valuing authenticity and unique perspectives, driving our spirit of innovation. We foster an inclusive culture where diversity isn't just a goal but a part of our values and way of working. This is how we do business for a sustainable future.  Learn more at www.epiroc.com (https://javascript:void(0);)

Job Description

Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. is the world leader in serving science, with annual revenue of approximately $40 billion.

Our Mission is to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. Whether our customers are accelerating life sciences research, solving complex analytical challenges, increasing productivity in their laboratories, improving patient health through diagnostics or the development and manufacture of life-changing therapies, we are here to support them.

Our team  of more than 100,000 colleagues delivers an unrivaled combination of innovative technologies, purchasing convenience and pharmaceutical services through our industry-leading brands, including Thermo Scientific, Applied Biosystems, Invitrogen, Fisher Scientific, Unity Lab Services, Patheon and PPD.

For our site in Wuppertal, we are looking for a

Senior Finance Analyst (m/f/d) – Manufacturing Finance

The Senior Finance Analyst (m/d/d) will be a key business partner to the Manufacturing, Operations and Supply Chain teams, supporting financial planning, month-end close activities and operational decision making to improve Wuppertal site performance.

Working closely with the Site Finance Manager, the role will take ownership of key finance processes and assigned areas, providing independent financial analysis, insights and recommendations to support business performance.

The position requires a strong combination of manufacturing finance expertise, analytical capabilities and business partnering skills, with the ability to operate independently and progressively take on broader responsibilities within site finance.

A day in the Life:

- Partner directly with Operations, Manufacturing and Supply Chain teams, providing financial insights, constructively challenging assumptions and supporting operational decision making.
- Analyse transactional and operational data, identify trends, anomalies, risks and opportunities, and translate findings into clear conclusions and actionable recommendations.
- Support financial performance reviews for assigned areas and communicate key findings and recommendations to Finance and operational stakeholders.
- Contribute to post-acquisition integration activities and the implementation and adoption of new systems and standardized processes, including SAP, Oracle and other finance tools.
- Build strong cross-functional relationships and independently manage assigned finance topics end-to-end, escalating material risks and decisions to the Site Finance Manager as appropriate.riate.

Keys to Success:

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance plus 5+ years of progressive and relevant professional experience in Manufacturing Finance, preferably within an international manufacturing environment.
- ·Strong understanding of manufacturing finance and business processes, including manufacturing costs, standard costing, variance analysis, inventory, absorption, accruals, budgeting and forecasting.
- Demonstrated ability to independently manage assigned finance areas and processes end-to-end, from analysis and problem identification through recommendation and follow-up.
- Proficient user of finance and analytical systems such as SAP, Oracle, Power BI and Excel. Experience with ERP implementation or migration projects is considered an advantage.

What we offer:

- Employment with an innovative, future-oriented organisation
- Outstanding career and development prospects
- Company pension scheme and other fringe benefits
- ·Exciting company culture which stands for integrity, intensity, involvement and innovation

If you are interested, please apply online with your CV and Motivation Letter, References including possible start date and salary expectations.

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, each one of our 100,000 extraordinary minds has a unique story to tell. Join us and contribute to our singular mission—enabling our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer.

Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of  , color, religion, ___ ,   orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or any other legally protected status.

Apply today! http://jobs.thermofisher.com (http://jobs.thermofisher.com)

Agency notice!

Please note we are not interested in receiving unsolicited CVs from any personnel service providers. Should you choose to send us or upload any such candidate document they will not be acknowledged and will be deleted in line with our privacy policy.

Your challenge

- Product Compliance: Ensure semiconductor manufacturing equipment meets EU Machinery Regulation (EU 2023/1230), LVD, EMC, and SEMI standards.
- Conformity Assessment: Conduct product conformity assessments following CE, UL, and SEMI safety standards, and comply with regional standards where AIXTRON operates.

- Risk Assessments: Conduct safety risk assessments in line with ISO 12100 and Chemical Risk Assessments for product development and modifications of existing product lines.

- Technical Consultation: Contribute to the design of gas mixing system and vacuum system, advising on safety requirements related to piping and instrumentation diagrams, electrical diagrams and control systems.

- Experience: More than 4 years of work experience in process safety, chemical kinetics and thermodynamics.
- Certifications: Process safety or risk management certification is added advantage.
- Technical Expertise: Experience in process safety management by implementing process safety principle to minimize risks associated with chemical handling. Review advanced thermodynamics for energy management and safety assessment.
- Communication: Strong communication skills with confidence in presentations and technical consulting.
- Teamwork and Adaptability: Highly motivated and adaptable team player with a strong analytical mindset and structured working style. Excellent organizational skills and a passion for interdisciplinary engineering projects.

- Health: We are committed to providing support for your physical and mental health, e.g., through regular health campaigns.
- Personal development: It is important to us that you continue to evolve your skills, be it with the help of our own AIXTRON Academy or through personalized development programs.
- Corporate Benefits: As part of our Corporate Benefits program, you benefit from exclusive discounts with numerous partner companies.
- Retirement benefits and additional insurance: We support your retirement planning and offer capital-forming benefits as well as individual supplementary insurance options.
- Catering: In our company cafeteria, you can enjoy subsidized meals as well as fresh seasonal fruit baskets.
- Open corporate culture: We foster an open and respectful culture – first-name terms – that extends across all hierarchical levels.
- Sustainability and mobility: We are committed to sustainability and provide EV charging stations for cars and bicycles, as well as convenient transport connections and free parking spaces.
- Employee referral program: If you help attract new talent to AIXTRON, we will reward you generously through our employee referral program.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher (m,f,x) in Computational Neuroscience (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for a

Postdoctoral Researcher (m,f,x) in Computational Neuroscience

The Collaborative Research Center 1280 “Extinction Learning” (SFB 1280) is an interdisciplinary research consortium investigating the neural, cognitive, and behavioral mechanisms underlying extinction learning. Its 19 subprojects bring together researchers from neuroscience, psychology, medicine, and computational modeling across six research locations. The consortium is coordinated at Ruhr University Bochum (RUB). The Computational Neuroscience group at the Institute for Neural Computation at RUB investigates the neural and computational mechanisms underlying learning, episodic memory, and spatial navigation. Within SFB 1280, we use computational modeling to develop mechanistic accounts of learning and memory and work closely with experimental research groups to relate model dynamics to neural and behavioral data. Further information can be found at https://www.rub.de/cns

We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to investigate the neural mechanisms underlying episodic memory and spatial navigation. The successful candidate will develop quantitative spiking neural network models of the hippocampus in an interdisciplinary and collaborative research environment. The project aims to understand how hippocampal sequences during sharp-wave ripples (SWRs) are generated and how they are shaped by previous experience and neuromodulatory influences to support memory consolidation. Computational models will be developed in close interaction with experimental collaborators and validated against in vivo electrophysiological and behavioral data from rodents.

Scope: full-time
Duration: fixed-term, until 30.06.2029 (end of project)
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-10-19

Your tasks:

- Develop and investigate quantitative spiking neural network models of hippocampal circuits involved in episodic memory and spatial navigation.
- Model how learning and previous experience shape hippocampal representations and sequence generation.
- Derive quantitative predictions from computational models that can be tested using experimental data.
- Analyze and integrate in vivo electrophysiological and behavioral data from rodents to constrain, test, and validate computational models.
- Work closely with experimental collaborators to establish an iterative exchange between computational modeling and empirical research.
- Present research findings at national and international conferences and workshops.
- Publish research results in international peer-reviewed journals.
- Contribute to the supervision and scientific mentoring of doctoral, master’s, and bachelor’s students where appropriate. (At the request of the applicant, participation in teaching is possible.)

Your profile:

- A successfully completed PhD in computational neuroscience, physics, computer science, cognitive science, or a closely related field
- A strong quantitative background and demonstrated experience in computational or mathematical modeling, preferably including biologically plausible or spiking neural network models
- Strong programming skills, preferably in Python, and experience with scientific computing and numerical simulations
- Ability to conduct research independently, develop new research questions, and take responsibility for the implementation and analysis of computational studies
- Excellent communication and teamwork skills and enthusiasm for close collaboration with experimental neuroscientists
- Excellent written and spoken English
- Experience with modern software development practices, version control, high-performance computing, and reproducible research workflows is an advantag

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Developmental Psychology (75% position, E13 TV-L salary scale) (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.87 hours/week = 75%) from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for 1

PhD Position in Developmental Psychology (75% position, E13 TV-L salary scale) – Starting January 1, 2027

The Chair of Developmental Psychology at Ruhr-Universität Bochum invites applications for a position as a research associate (m/f/x) within a research project on the development of episodic memory in early childhood. The project will be conducted in close collaboration at two locations: Bochum and Dortmund. The successful candidate will contribute to the planning, execution, analysis, and publication of a longitudinal study involving children aged 3 to 5 years at the research site in Bochum. The project is embedded in a Collaborative Research Centre (CRC). The CRC “Episodic Memory” is an interdisciplinary consortium consisting of researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy and neuroscience. The basis for our research is the Scenario Construction Framework which conceptualizes scenarios as mental simulations of past episodes, constructed from episodic memory traces and semantic information. As a member of this team, you will be trained in interdisciplinary research and have access to a broad spectrum of initiatives to support you in your academic journey. The CRC will be housed at the new research building THINK in Bochum, which is not only equipped with cutting edge technology, but also houses a childcare area (which includes, e.g., an outside play area, bedroom), parent child offices, common rooms to foster networking, etc. The position offers the opportunity for scientific qualification through a cumulative PhD. Employment is subject to final approval and funding by the third-party funding provider.

Scope: part-time
Duration: fixed-term, until 31.12.2030 (end of project)
Start: from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval
Apply by:  2026-10-26

Your tasks:

- Design, implementation, analysis, and publication of studies on the development of episodic memory in early childhood
- (Co-)supervision of student assistants and research students
- Proactive interdisciplinary collaboration and exchange within and beyond the CRC throughout the research process
- Presentation of study results at internal and external events and scientific conferences
- Active participation in CRC events
- Regular contribution to public relations and science communication

Your profile:

Required:

- A Master’s degree in Psychology or a closely related field
- A strong interest in developmental psychology research on memory and enthusiasm for scientific work
- A highly motivated team player who enjoys collaborating with researchers from various disciplines, particularly in the areas of modeling, philosophy, and neuroscience
- Proactive problem-solver in daily work
- Enjoyment of interacting with parents and children in a research context
- Fluent proficiency in German and English (written and spoken)
- Excellent methodological, programming, and statistical skills

Desired

- Practical experience working with infants and young children in a research context
- Prior experience in interdisciplinary research settings

jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.87 hours/week = 75%;) from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for 1

PhD position in computational neuroscience

The Department of Social Neuroscience at the Faculty of Medicine is part of the Research Center One Health Ruhr of the University Alliance Ruhr and investigates the neurobiological mechanisms underlying social processes in humans. Our laboratory combines neuroimaging methods, including fMRI, fNIRS, and mobile EEG, with psychophysiological recordings, hormonal assessments, and experimental behavioral approaches.

The PhD candidate will investigate the neural mechanisms of socially distributed episodic memory through experimental studies, data collection and analysis, and collaboration within the CRC 1844 research environment.

Scope: part-time
Duration: fixed-term, 31.12.2030 (end of project)
Start: from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval
Apply by:  2026-10-26

Your tasks:

- Conducting experimental studies on social interaction and episodic memory
- Collection and analysis of behavioral, fMRI, and fNIRS data
- Presentation of research findings at national and international scientific conferences
- Publication of results in international peer-reviewed journals
- Active participation in the scientific activities and training program of CRC 1844
- Co-supervision of research assistants and student theses

Your profile:

- A very good university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in psychology, cognitive neuroscience, neuroscience, or a related field
- Strong interest in social neuroscience, episodic memory, and neuroimaging
- Very good knowledge of research methods and statistics
- High level of commitment, reliability, and ability to work independently as well as collaboratively
- Very good command of written and spoken English
- Previous experience with one or more project-relevant methods, particularly fMRI or fNIRS, is an advantage but not mandatory

jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.87 hours/week = 75%) from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for 1

PhD position (f/m/d) in TMS-EEG of episodic memory

The Collaborative Research Center “Episodic Memory” (CRC 1844) is an interdisciplinary consortium consisting of researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy and neuroscience. The basis for our research is the Scenario Construction Framework which conceptualizes scenarios as mental simulations of past episodes, constructed from episodic memory traces and semantic information. As a part of this team, you will be trained in interdisciplinary research and have access to a broad spectrum of initiatives to support you in your academic journey. The CRC will be housed at the new research building THINK in Bochum, which is not only equipped with cutting edge technology, but also houses a child care area (which includes, e.g., an outside play area, bedroom), parent child offices, common rooms to foster networking, etc. Within the CRC1844, the Computational Neurology group led by Prof. Dr. Xenia Kobeleva, investigates clinically relevant questions in neuropsychiatry and neurodegenerative diseases using advanced computational approaches, neuroimaging, and neurostimulation. The group is situated in the Institute for Neural Computation and is part of the Bernstein Node Bochum of the Science Hub Neuroscience. Our group works at the interface of clinical neuroscience (neurostimulation and neurodegenerative diseases) and computational neuroscience, with a strong focus on translational research that connects computational methods to real-world clinical data and patient-oriented questions. Our team is young, motivated, international, and genuinely interdisciplinary, bringing together expertise from medicine, neuroscience, psychology, and quantitative sciences. Besides a direct connection to clinical neurology, we are intensively collaborating with world-leading experts for mathematics, psychology, and computer science. The proposed PhD position will focus on the following project: Regions within the cortico-hippocampal network display interactions with the prefrontal cortex during episodic memory. To understand network effects, we will conduct an EEG memory task modulated by transcranial magnetic stimulation, studied by Bayesian modeling and EEG oscillatory analysis.

Scope: part-time
Duration: fixed-term, until 31.12.2030 (end of project)
Start: from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval
Apply by:  2026-10-19

Your tasks:

- Independently conduct fMRI and TMS-EEG experiments to better understand and modulate episodic memory
- Preprocess and analyze the resulting neuroimaging data (including oscillatory analysis)
- Presentation of research results at national and international conferences
- Publication of research results in scientific journals

Your profile:

- You are genuinely curious and interested in exploring how the brain works and what can be done to fix it in case of disorders. You can solve problems in a creative way and like to define research gaps by looking across applied and theoretical research. You have experience in interaction both with experimental and theoretical scientists and you have ability to work both independently and as part of an interdisciplinary team.
- We are looking for highly motivated candidates with a Master’s degree in medicine, neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology, biology, biomedical engineering, and related fields.
- Necessary prerequisites are prior practical experience in executing neuroscientific neuroimaging or neurostimulation experiments, preferably using TMS, fMRI, or EEG.
- It is a plus if you are experienced with neuroimaging analysis tools (e.g., MNE-Python, EEGLAB) and statistical tools (R, Stata or similar) or programming (ideally Python).
- We also expect strong analytical skills, ability for independent, creative and critical thinking, and excellent communication and writing skills in the English language. Also, German language skills are a plus but not a requirement.

State-of-the-art AI systems depend heavily on models, providers and hardware from the U.S. and China, which represents a big challenge of Europe’s sovereignty for AI model development and deployment (e.g., trustworthiness, dependability, performance, modularity). The Horizon Europe project OptimAIse (Optimising Performance and Trust for Integrity-driven Modular genAI Software Engineering) addresses these challenges by delivering a scalable, modular, and interoperable reference architecture that leverages European hardware to enable efficient and simplified large language model deployments. The SpiNNaker2 hardware, developed by TU Dresden and commercialized by SpiNNcloud, is one of Europe’s most promising alternatives for the energy-efficient serving of LLMs. SpiNNaker2 is a massively parallel architecture with locally dense compute and globally sparse and low-latency communication, ideal to realize efficient AI models by leveraging sparse and event-based computing.

The candidate will develop and adopt LLMs for the SpiNNaker2 hardware. The models shall be implemented on the hardware using an existing software stack and optimized with ML compilers such as MLIR. Besides applying known approaches such as Mixture-of-Experts, the candidate shall follow the state of the art of efficient language models and try novel approaches on SpiNNaker2. In addition, the work will derive requirements and recommendation for next-generation AI hardware such as Spinnaker3, thus guiding the future of efficient AI systems.

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest cancers, largely because its dense stromal and immune microenvironment drives therapy resistance that conventional cell-line models and 3D organoids fail to capture. In this joint project, we are looking for a PhD candidate to characterise an ex vivo PDAC tissue model that preserves native tissue architecture together with the stromal and immune compartments, and to develop it into a working platform for drug testing and screening. The successful candidate will be jointly supervised by both groups and fully embedded in each - a rare opportunity to combine pathology, tumour biology and pharmacology within one project.
